sentences.en: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 你好,这是6分钟英语 从英国广播公司学习英语。

sentences.en: I'm Pippa. And I'm Phil. What was your favourite game when you were a child, Pippa?
sentences.zh: 我是皮帕,我是菲尔 你小时候最喜欢什么游戏,皮帕?

sentences.en: I think my favourite game was skipping with a skipping rope.
sentences.zh: 我想我最喜欢的游戏是跳过 与跳绳。

sentences.en: How about you? Well, I could never skip, so I think I just preferred playing football.
sentences.zh: 我从不跳,所以我更喜欢打橄榄球

sentences.en: Ahh! Well, that's a good game to play in the playground.
sentences.zh: 这游戏在游乐场玩得真好

sentences.en: Eighty years ago, it was quite common for children in Britain's cities to play in bombsites, the ruins of houses which had been destroyed in World War II.
sentences.zh: 80年前,英国城市的儿童经常在炸弹中玩耍,这是第二次世界大战摧毁的房屋的废墟。

sentences.en: Today the idea is back in fashion, with kids playing not in bombsites but in 'junk playgrounds', also called 'adventure playgrounds'.
sentences.zh: 今天这个想法又回到了时尚状态, 孩子们不玩炸弹,而是玩“垃圾场”, 也叫“冒险游戏场”。

sentences.en: In contrast to pre-made playgrounds, where swings and slides are fixed in place, adventure playgrounds provide pieces of building materials for kids to build things themselves.
sentences.zh: 与预设的游乐场相比,摇摆和幻灯片是固定的,冒险游乐场为孩子们自己建造东西提供了建筑材料。

sentences.en: Reporter William Kremer went to see one such playground in Wrexham, North Wales, for BBC World Service programme People Fixing the World: At first glance,the land is little more than a junkyard.
sentences.zh: 记者William Kremer在北威尔士的Wrexham为英国广播公司世界服务节目《人们修复世界:看一看,这块土地只不过是一个垃圾场。

sentences.en: There are stacks of used wooden pallets and big reels for holding wires.
sentences.zh: 有一堆用过的木质货盘和大鱼雷,用来装有铁丝网。

sentences.en: But if you look a little bit closer, you'll see crooked homemade structures, hidey-holes and turrets.
sentences.zh: 但如果你再近一点看 你会看到弯曲的自制结构 隐蔽的洞穴和炮塔

sentences.en: Children run barefoot. They swing on ropes and throw themselves down a makeshift water slide.
sentences.zh: 孩子们赤脚跑 挥舞绳子 跳下临时滑水

sentences.en: At first glance, William sees only junk.
sentences.zh: 初看起来 威廉只看到垃圾

sentences.en: The phrase at first glance means looking at something for the first time, before having a chance to look more carefully.
sentences.zh: 初见之明的意思是,在有机会更仔细地审视之前,第一次审视一些东西。

sentences.en: Adventure playgrounds are indeed full of junk: pieces of construction material like old tyres, planks of wood and lengths of rope.
sentences.zh: 冒险游乐场确实充满了垃圾:建筑材料,如旧轮胎、木板和绳子长度。

sentences.en: But look closely and you'll see children using the junk to play, building dens and hidey-holes.
sentences.zh: 但仔细看,你会看到孩子们 利用垃圾玩耍, 建造洞穴和隐藏洞。

sentences.en: A hidey-hole is a small place for hiding things or, in this case, for children to hide themselves.
sentences.zh: 一个隐蔽的洞是一个隐藏东西的小地方,或者,在这种情况下,儿童可以隐藏自己。

sentences.en: In this episode, we'll be hearing how adventure playgrounds are giving kids the freedom and space to play.
sentences.zh: 在这集中,我们将会听到冒险游乐场是如何给孩子们自由与空间玩耍的。

sentences.en: As usual, we'll be learning some useful new words and phrases.
sentences.zh: 和往常一样,我们会学习一些有用的新词句

sentences.en: And remember – you can find all this episode's vocabulary, along with a transcript, on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 记住,你可以在我们的网站上 找到这集的词汇,还有笔录,bbc学习英语。com。

sentences.en: But now I have a question for you, Pippa.
sentences.zh: 现在我有个问题要问你 皮帕

sentences.en: We know that adventure playgrounds started off after the Second World War, but in which country?
sentences.zh: 我们知道,冒险游乐场是在第二次世界大战之后开始的,但在哪个国家?

sentences.en: Was it: a) France, b) Germany, or c) Denmark?
sentences.zh: 是:a) 法国,b) 德国,或c) 丹麦?

sentences.en: Hmm… I think maybe France. I think French children maybe were very adventurous.
sentences.zh: 嗯,我想也许法国,我觉得法国孩子可能很冒险

sentences.en: OK. Well, we'll find out the answer to that question later in the programme.
sentences.zh: 好吧,我们稍后在节目中 找出这个问题的答案

sentences.en: Adventure playgrounds give kids the freedom to choose how they play.
sentences.zh: 冒险游乐场让孩子们有选择游戏方式的自由

sentences.en: According to child development expert Dr Anna Housley Juster, this freedom is vital, as she explains here to BBC World Service's People Fixing the World: It's true.
sentences.zh: 据儿童发展专家Anna Houssley Juster博士说,

sentences.en: We do tend to minimise play in certain ways, but actually after the most basic needs are met for children – so, food, shelter, water, safe place to be – play is by far the most important factor for healthy child development.
sentences.zh: 我们确实倾向于以某些方式尽量减少游戏,但实际上,在满足儿童最基本的需求之后(因此,食物、住所、水、安全的地方),游戏是儿童健康成长的最重要因素。

sentences.en: Anna thinks play is as important as a child's basic needs, like food and safety, but unfortunately the importance of play tends to be minimised.
sentences.zh: Anna认为游戏与儿童的基本需要一样重要, 比如食物和安全, 但不幸的是游戏的重要性往往被最小化。

sentences.en: If something tends to happen, it happens often and is likely to happen again.
sentences.zh: 如果有事情发生,它经常发生,而且可能再次发生。

sentences.en: Anna says that after a child's basic needs are met, play is by far the most important factor in a healthy childhood.
sentences.zh: Anna说,在满足儿童的基本需要之后,玩耍是健康童年最重要的因素。

sentences.en: She uses the phrase by far to mean by a great amount.
sentences.zh: 她用这个词来形容很多东西

sentences.en: For example, your teacher might say, "You're by far the best student in class!"
sentences.zh: 比如说,你的老师可能会说, "你们是班里最好的学生!"

sentences.en: The freedom to take controlled risks in a safe environment is what Anna calls 'self-directed play'.
sentences.zh: 在安全的环境中 自由承担受控风险 是安娜所说的"自制游戏"

sentences.en: Here, she explains more to Myra Anubi, presenter of BBC programme People Fixing the World: So, what you're saying is letting kids play… free play actually, or play on their own and, kind of, come up with the ideas – that's really crucial for their development.
sentences.zh: 她向BBC节目《改变世界》的主持人Myra Anubi解释更多: 所以,你的意思是让孩子们玩... 自由游戏,或者自己玩, 以及,比如说,想出一些想法-- 这对他们的发展至关重要。

sentences.en: It's one hundred percent crucial for their development.
sentences.zh: 百分之百地对他们的发展至关重要。

sentences.en: In… what I meant when I said that it's protective is that kids build resiliency, confidence, coping strategies, regulation strategies.
sentences.zh: 我指的是 孩子们建立复原力 信心 应对策略 调控策略

sentences.en: So many of the skills that we know lead to healthy human development are developed in play.
sentences.zh: 我们所知道的导致人类健康发展的许多技能都是在发挥作用。

sentences.en: Myra mentions the importance of free play and Anna says it's one hundred percent crucial, meaning completely.
sentences.zh: Myra提到自由游戏的重要性 Anna说百分之百关键 意思是完全的

sentences.en: You can also say, " One hundred percent," as an informal response to mean: "Yes, I agree with you completely."
sentences.zh: 你也可以说,"百分之百," 作为非正式的回答 意思是:"是的,我完全同意你。"

sentences.en: Adventure playgrounds have lots of small dangers: hard pieces of wood, sharp metal, nails.
sentences.zh: 冒险游乐场有很多小危险:硬木、尖金属、钉子。

sentences.en: According to Anna, taking small risks when playing with these makes kids more resilient and builds coping strategies – a term for the psychological ways children develop to manage challenging situations.
sentences.zh: Anna认为,在玩耍这些游戏时承担小风险可以让孩子更有韧性,并构建应对策略 — — 儿童在心理上发展出应对挑战的心理方式。

sentences.en: And Phil, I think it's time for the answer to your quiz question.
sentences.zh: 菲尔,我想是时候回答你的问题了

sentences.en: Yes, I asked you in which country adventure playgrounds started.
sentences.zh: 是的,我问你 在哪个国家冒险游乐场开始。

sentences.en: You said France, but I'm afraid the correct answer was Denmark.
sentences.zh: 你说的法国,但我担心正确的答案是丹麦。

sentences.en: They were introduced by Danish architect Carl Theodor Sorensen.
sentences.zh: 他们由丹麦建筑师卡尔·西奥多·索伦森介绍。

sentences.en: OK. Let's recap the vocabulary we've learned, starting with the phrase at first glance – when you see something quickly, without a chance to consider it more carefully.
sentences.zh: 好吧,让我们回顾一下我们所学的词汇,从第一眼的短语开始,当你们很快看到一些东西时,没有机会更仔细地考虑它。

sentences.en: A hidey-hole is a small place for hiding things in, or hiding yourself in.
sentences.zh: 隐藏的洞是一个小地方 隐藏的东西, 或隐藏自己。

sentences.en: If people tend to do something, they do it often and will probably continue to do it in the future.
sentences.zh: 如果人们倾向于做一些事情,他们经常这样做,而且将来可能还会继续这样做。

sentences.en: The phrase by far means by a great amount.
sentences.zh: 这个词的意义远非如此。

sentences.en: Saying one hundred percent means completely and can be used to emphasise a statement or show that you totally agree with it.
sentences.zh: 说百分之百意味着完全 并且可以用来强调 声明或表明 你完全同意它。

sentences.en: And finally, coping strategies are psychological ways of managing your emotions in challenging situations.
sentences.zh: 最后,应对策略是心理上的方法 来管理你的情绪 在充满挑战的情况下。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up, but remember – you can find many more trending topics, plus a quiz and worksheet for this episode, on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 我们的六分钟又到了, 但请记住——你可以在网站上找到更多热门话题,

sentences.en: Hope to see you there soon, but for now it's goodbye.
sentences.zh: 希望很快能见到你 但现在是再见了

sentences.en: Goodbye!
sentences.zh: 再见!
